metadata.subject: Biology
metadata.topic: Plant Biology — Balanced Chemical Equation for Photosynthesis
metadata.note: Q2a(i) 'define photosynthesis' is open-ended — not auto-gradeable. This file covers only Q2a(ii). 2 marks awarded: 1 mark for correctly balanced reactants, 1 mark for correctly balanced products.

question.name: CSEC Bio Jan 2024 Q2a(ii) — Balanced Equation for Photosynthesis
question.text: Write a balanced chemical equation for the process of photosynthesis by completing the equation below. Drag the correct coefficient or formula into each blank.
question.general_feedback:
Balanced equation:

6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂

(Requires light energy and chlorophyll — often shown above the arrow)

Reactants (1 mark): 6CO₂ + 6H₂O — six molecules of carbon dioxide and six of water
Products (1 mark): C₆H₁₂O₆ (glucose) + 6O₂ — one glucose molecule and six oxygen molecules

Key check: Count atoms: Left: 6C, 12H, 18O — Right: 6C + 12H + 6O + 6O = 6C, 12H, 18O ✓

groups.label: Coefficient of CO₂
groups.diagnostic_hint: Count the carbon atoms: glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) has 6 carbons, so you need 6 CO₂ molecules on the left side.

groups.label: Coefficient of H₂O
groups.diagnostic_hint: Count the hydrogen atoms: glucose has 12 H, and each H₂O provides 2 H, so you need 6 H₂O molecules.

groups.label: Glucose formula
groups.diagnostic_hint: Glucose is a 6-carbon monosaccharide with the molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₆. C₃H₆O₃ is a 3-carbon sugar (half a glucose); C₆H₁₂O₃ has the wrong oxygen count.

groups.label: Coefficient of O₂
groups.diagnostic_hint: Count the oxygen atoms on the right: glucose has 6 O, and you need a total of 18 O (from 6 CO₂ on the left). 18 − 6 = 12 O needed as O₂ → 6 O₂ molecules.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 9 tokens for 4 slots. Key distractors: C₃H₆O₃ (half-glucose/3-carbon sugar confusing students who know glycolysis); C₆H₁₂O₃ (wrong H:O ratio); 12 (common error for water coefficient from confusion with 12H₂O in C4 plants or light-dependent reactions); ATP (high-value distractor for students who know ATP is produced but confuse it with glucose).
